subject: Hotline: Everly Health throughput regression & exec bridge
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: HOT: Everly Health - spike in p50/p95 latency and 5xx rate since 08:45 PT

Team —

Alert from Everly at 08:50 PT: they're seeing a sustained spike in generation latency (p95 ~ 2.8s -> 7.2s) and a bump in 5xx errors for the last 45m. Their traffic pattern is normal; the surge correlates with longer average prompt lengths this morning but we haven't seen model-side queueing explain the 5xx spike.

Initial asks:
- Vivek: can you triage kernel/resource saturation on the dedicated pool serving everly-prod and check infra-side error logs (OOM, gRPC disconnects)?
- Rishi: loop in infra-oncall and surface any config rollouts or autoscaler flaps since 07:30 PT.
- Logan: please confirm impact severity and PST exec availability for a 30–45m bridge. Customer says it's causing timeouts in their checkout flow.

I'm attaching a quick latency screenshot from their dashboard and the signed SLA for reference. We'll escalate to an exec bridge if we can't stabilize in 30m.

Attachments: latency-dash-20260730.png, SLA-commitments-Everly-2026.pdf

--
Marissa Cole
Senior CSM, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-30T09:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HOT: Everly Health - spike in p50/p95 latency and 5xx rate since 08:45 PT

Marissa — quick update from triage:
- Observed elevated GPU utilization on pool-redwood-ded-7 serving everly-prod (~86% -> 98% over 25m).
- KV cache hit rate dropped ~12% correlating with a rolling cache invalidation job that executed at 08:40 PT (internal job INF-1137).
- Error stream shows increased gRPC DEADLINE_EXCEEDED and a handful of memcopy timeout traces; no obvious OOMs.

Actions taken:
1) Scoped eviction window on cache job and paused subsequent invalidations.
2) Triggered a burst scale (manual) to add two GPU workers to the pool — provisioning in progress (ETA ~7m).
3) Increased gRPC timeouts on the gateway for this route as a temporary mitigation.

I'll post logs and the sequence of related kernel warnings to INF-1137. If provisioning completes and cache stabilizes, latency should drop; if not, we need an exec bridge.

-Vivek
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-30T09:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HOT: Everly Health - spike in p50/p95 latency and 5xx rate since 08:45 PT

Marissa / team —

Rajesh (Everly VP Eng) just replied: their checkout retries are now failing ~15% of the time which is causing customer-visible errors. They're on a high-profile roll (marketing campaign) so urgency is high; he asked for a bridge with Redwood execs (sales + eng) within the hour.

Customer availability: Rajesh can do 10:15 PT or 11:00 PT for an exec bridge. He also asked for a temporary routing bypass to our lower-latency model variant if possible.

I recommend we accept 10:15 PT and include Laura for exec-level commitments.

-Logan
From: Rajesh Patel <r.patel@everly-health.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@everly-health.com
Date: 2026-07-30T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in latency and errors — Everly production

Marissa —

Thanks for the quick flag. To reiterate impact: roughly 14% of checkout API calls retry and surface a 502 back to users (mobile + web). Our ops team is throttling traffic to mitigate user-visible failures but that's impacting conversion. This is a P0 for us while the campaign is live.

We appreciate the burst attempt; if there's a safe temporary model routing to a slightly older/reduced-latency variant that preserves output quality, we'd accept that while you stabilize the pool. Also want a clear ETA on a rollback/timeline for a full mitigation.

-Rajesh
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-30T09:50:00-07:00
Subject: Exec bridge confirmed — 10:15 PT (30m) — Everly Health P0

Team —

Quick status and plan before execs:
- Current: manual burst scale in progress (Vivek). Cache invalidation job paused (Vivek). We see partial improvement in p50 but p95 still elevated.
- Customer impact: 14% checkout retries/502s, high-visibility campaign. Rajesh has confirmed 10:15 PT bridge.

Bridge invite: Zoom + slack channel (link in related_links). Laura — please be on the bridge to authorize any temporary customer concessions (credits/priority SLAs). Rishi / Vivek — be ready to present root-cause hypothesis and fallbacks (model routing, routing to different region, emergency fallback model). Logan — you own customer comms on the bridge and confirm post-bridge messaging.

Pre-reads attached (SLA excerpt) and an annotated latency snapshot. I'll open the Zoom and post the bridge notes to INF-1137.

If we cannot restore within the bridge window, we need an agreed customer-facing mitigation (routing to variant + temporary credit).

-Marissa
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Patel <r.patel@everly-health.com>, support@everly-health.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-30T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Post-bridge summary and next steps — Everly P0

Rajesh / Everly team — thanks for joining the 10:15 PT bridge. Summary of outcomes and next steps: 

1) What happened: an automated cache invalidation job (INF-1137) ran at 08:40 PT and coincided with a small surge in average prompt length from an A/B test; the combination reduced KV hits and temporarily saturated the dedicated pool. That led to increased gateway timeouts and elevated p95.

2) Immediate mitigations applied during the bridge:
   - Paused cache invalidation job and rolled back the job change (Vivek)
   - Manual burst scale added two GPU workers and stabilized queueing (Vivek)
   - Temporarily increased gateway timeouts for the route (Vivek)
   - Enabled routing to our lower-latency model variant for Everly (agreed; temporary)

3) Impact metrics (post-mitigation): p95 reduced to ~2.1s within 20m, 5xx rate returned to baseline by ~11:05 PT, checkout failure rate dropped from 14% -> 1.6%.

4) Follow-ups / owners / ETA:
   - Engineering (Vivek / Rishi) to harden cache invalidation orchestration and add a safety window: deliverable by 2026-08-06.
   - Platform (Rishi) to add autoscaler alarm thresholds tuned to prompt-length volatility: deliverable by 2026-08-04.
   - Customer success (Marissa / Logan) to coordinate formal write-up and any commercial gestures (credit proposal) by 2026-08-02.

5) Commercial note: Laura, please advise on credit range; we discussed a 20–30% credit on affected tokens as a starting point for negotiation.

6) Docs / tickets: full bridge notes and logs are attached to INF-1137 and the Drive folder (related_links).

We will follow up with a short RCA and timeline-oriented action plan. Apologies for the disruption and thanks for your patience — we prioritize reliability for Everly.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior CSM, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
